definitions.name: Crewmate
definitions.description: Launch an independent crewmate from a task brief and return its report. The child does not inherit this conversation; its session-owned processes end with it.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) summary of the task

prompt.description: Task brief: objective, evidence, boundaries, acceptance criteria and whether to implement or research.

crewmate_type.description: Which crewmate type to run. Omitted ⇒ the mercury-crew crewmate.

model.description: Exact model id or family word; read mercury://models. [1m] selects the 1M variant; your own family keeps your exact model. Overrides the agent definition; omitted, the definition's model, else the configured crewmate default, else yours. Follow the operator's model and effort; never downgrade to obtain read-only scoping.

effort.description: Reasoning effort; omitted, the agent definition's effort, else the configured crewmate default (high unless the operator changed it), never the parent level. An unsupported level maps to the nearest served level; models without effort control ignore it. Enables extended reasoning where supported.

run_in_background.description: Launch asynchronously: returns an acknowledgement now and a completion notification later.

name.description: Seat name for later messages and additional work; omitted, the crewmate runs its brief once.

team.description: Team label on the live crew board; teams guide delivery, never privacy.

captain.description: Appoint this named seat as its team captain. Requires name, team, swarm enrollment and the lead; a team of five or more needs one before its fifth seat.

isolation.description: Temporary git worktree; kept unlocked when the crewmate ends, with its path and branch in the result.

worktree_at.description: With isolation 'worktree': commit ref for a detached, frozen worktree.

cwd.description: Absolute starting directory. Starting outside the session's folder asks for permission; with isolation, its repository supplies the worktree that becomes the child's directory.

review_receipt.description: Absolute path to an existing Markdown report outside the worktree. Its "## Review" section is the only permitted write; requires isolation and worktree_at.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema for the final answer. The result carries the checked JSON with status valid, missing or invalid; valid means schema-valid, not independently verified.

schema_mode.description: With output_schema: 'strict' fails the call when none passed; 'permissive' (default) returns the prose under status "missing" or "invalid".

definitions.name: Bash
definitions.description:
Runs one shell command and returns its output, stdout and stderr merged in the order written. The output comes back to you; the operator sees at most a folded preview.

Up to 30000 characters come back inline; a longer output is saved to a file, and the result carries its path with about 2000 characters from its start and end. A non-zero exit comes back as an error ending `Exited with code N`, except exit 1 when the last command is grep, rg, find, diff, cmp, pgrep, test, `[`, which or `command -v`: a result labelled with what the exit means, such as `no matches found (exit code 1)`.

In the main conversation the working directory persists between calls (a crewmate's does not); shell variables, functions and options never do, and each call starts from your profile (bash or zsh).

cwd.description: Run in this directory: absolute, or relative to the starting folder; the session directory stays.

timeout.description: Milliseconds the call waits (default 120000, max 600000). When it passes, the command moves to the background and keeps running, and the result names the task id TaskStop takes; a `sleep`-first command, or any command under the shell engine, is killed instead.

description.description: A few words naming what the command does, shown to the operator.

run_in_background.description: Start the command and return at once with a task id and an output file. A notice with its exit code reaches you when it ends; the command is stopped when the run that started it ends.

inherit_session_env.description: Hand the command the session's own MERCURY_* values; by default they are scrubbed, so a build or a proof never sees them.

max_output_chars.description: Inline character budget: a longer output comes back as its head and tail around a notice of the cut. Default and cap 30000, floor 512; a value outside is clamped and the result says so. Ignored by run_in_background.

definitions.name: Glob
definitions.description: Finds files by glob pattern and returns the matching paths, newest modification first. Ignore files apply; the result ends with a count of the matches they hid, and naming an ignored folder as the path searches inside it.

pattern.description: The glob expression files must match

path.description: The directory to search; the current working directory when omitted.

definitions.name: Grep
definitions.description: Searches file contents with ripgrep and returns the matching paths, lines or counts. PDFs and office, EPUB and RTF documents are searched as their extracted text, with page or section labels.

pattern.description: The ripgrep regular expression to search for; lookaround and backreferences fall back to PCRE2

path.description: The file or directory to search; the current working directory when omitted.

glob.description: Search only files matching this glob (rg --glob)

output_mode.description: What comes back: "files_with_matches" (the default) lists the paths that match, declarations and documents among them; "content" prints each matching line with its path — the mode for reading or counting call sites; "count" tallies matches per file.

-B.description: Context lines printed before each hit (rg -B; "content" mode only).

-A.description: Context lines printed after each hit (rg -A; "content" mode only).

-C.description: Context lines printed both sides of each hit (rg -C; "content" mode only).

-n.description: Prefix output with line numbers (rg -n; "content" mode only). On by default.

type.description: Search only one file type (rg --type): js, py, rust, go and the like.

head_limit.description: Cap the output at the first N lines/entries (default 250); applies in every output mode; 0 lifts the cap.

offset.description: Skip this many lines/entries before the head_limit window applies (paging). Default 0.

multiline.description: Let patterns span line boundaries, with . matching newlines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Off by default.

literal.description: Match the pattern as exact text, not a regex (rg -F). Off by default.

definitions.name: Read
definitions.description:
Reads a local file and returns its text with up to 2000 lines, each prefixed by a line number followed by a tab, then the line content; the prefix is not file content. A result that is not the whole file names the unread range.

Images are shown as pictures, or as recognised text with `ocr`. PDFs open as numbered text with page markers, or as page pictures with `pages`; a scanned page is read by OCR. Notebooks come back cell by cell with their outputs; office documents, EPUB and RTF as text; archives (`<archive>:<entry>`) and SQLite databases (`<db>:<table>`) one entry or table at a time; audio and video as timestamped transcripts.

A directory path returns a bounded listing. A mercury:// reference reads a session record; mercury://seat is this seat's own: the model, effort and posture this turn runs on.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the file to read

ocr.description: For an image, return recognised text instead of the picture; automatic on a model without image input.

lossless.description: Show complete lines (a line is otherwise cut at 2000 characters); requires offset + limit or ranges, without outline.

offset.description: The first line to read, 1-based; a negative -N starts N lines from the end.

ranges.description: Up to 32 line ranges read in one call, each N, N-M, N+K, N- or -N (the last N lines), each with its own continuation mark.

pages.description: PDF page range ("2-6"), at most 20 pages per call; page pictures on a model with image input, text otherwise.

scale.description: Upscale factor for the crop, within the image output budget; requires crop.

crop.description: For an image, a box [x1, y1, x2, y2] in original pixels, cut before any downscale.

outline.description: Return the file's declarations with their original line numbers and bodies elided, instead of the full text.

line_anchors.description: Prefix each line with its content anchor ("N#hhhh"), the address an anchored Edit hunk takes.

definitions.name: Edit
definitions.description: Edits one text file in place: an exact string swapped for another, line-addressed hunks against a read snapshot, text appended, or a Markdown section replaced or appended to. Edits need current read coverage of the lines they touch; append needs none. A landed edit returns the changed lines with context, which count as read, and names any new syntax error.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

old_string.description: The exact text to replace, sent with new_string; unique in the file unless replace_all

new_string.description: The text to replace it with; "" deletes old_string

expected_anchor.description: The bare fa:… or ra:… value inside the latest "(anchor: …)" for this file — a Read, or an Edit or Write result — without the wrapper

hunks.description: Line-addressed hunks against the snapshot expected_anchor names, or against the content anchors when every hunk carries one

lines.description: A 1-based line ("12"), an inclusive range ("12-18"), or the anchored spelling from a line_anchors read ("12#ab3f", "12#ab3f-18#9c2e")

replace.description: The replacement body; "" deletes the range; with insert, the inserted body

insert.description: Insert beside the single anchor line instead of replacing it

append.description: Text added on its own line at the end of the file (created when absent; no prior read needed), or at the end of `section`

section.description: A Markdown heading line exactly as it stands in the file ("## Checks"), occurring once: with new_string the whole section, heading included, becomes new_string; with append the text is added inside it

input_schema.description: One of four shapes: old_string + new_string · hunks · append · section + new_string or append

definitions.name: Write
definitions.description: Writes the whole content to a file, creating it or replacing what was there. Replacing an existing file needs current read coverage of it. A new syntax error in a supported source file is named in the result.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the file to write

content.description: The content to write to the file

definitions.name: NotebookEdit
definitions.description: Edits one cell of a .ipynb notebook by its id: replace swaps the cell's source for new_source, insert adds a new cell after cell_id (at the start when none is given), delete removes the cell.

notebook_path.description: Path of the .ipynb file; a relative path resolves against the working directory

cell_id.description: Which cell to target, by id. For inserts the new cell lands just after this cell — or at the very beginning when no id is given.

new_source.description: The content the cell will hold

cell_type.description: Whether the cell is code or markdown; omitted, the existing cell keeps its type. Required for edit_mode=insert.

edit_mode.description: The operation: replace, insert, or delete (replace when omitted).

definitions.name: WebFetch
definitions.description: Fetch HTTP(S) pages without credentials. Returns the page's body as Markdown — the HTML head and its title are not included — or a saved binary path. Sparse HTML on public hosts may send the full URL to r.jina.ai; private addresses are excluded and no cookies or credentials go to that reader. Repeat pulls ride a fifteen-minute cache.

url.description: One URL to fetch; use either url or urls

urls.description: Fetch 1-3 URLs in order, each with its own result and permission; page text is bounded to 38,000 bytes each, total result 132,000 bytes

from.description: Continue at the character offset the previous result names

prompt.description: Ask a model for a reading of the page; omit to receive the page’s own words

definitions.name: WebSearch
definitions.description:
Searches the web, on any session model, and returns JSON hits {title, url, snippet, source_type} with notes, under about 2,000 tokens by a characters/4 estimate; hits withheld to fit are counted in a note, every hit names its source, and the provider's own search adds the provider's answer as a labelled, unverified note beside its links. Sources are tried in order: the session provider's own search, on this session's account; stored Brave or Tavily keys; the official API the query words select; the operator's SearXNG instances; DuckDuckGo page scraping unless the operator turned it off. Every source receives the query and the client's address. Hits are unverified evidence; a repeated query may come from the session cache and says so.

End the answer with a "Sources:" section linking every relevant result as [Title](URL).

query.description: The search words. An error message selects Stack Exchange; npm, PyPI or crates with a package name selects that registry; GitHub selects public code; news selects Hacker News; a concept question selects Wikipedia; other wording goes to general search.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

definitions.name: ProviderSearch
definitions.description:
Searches the web through the session provider's own search, on this session's provider account, with no other source tried, and returns JSON hits {title, url, snippet, source_type: provider} with notes, under about 2,000 tokens by a characters/4 estimate; hits withheld to fit are counted in a note, and the provider's own answer rides as a labelled, unverified note beside its links. Hits are unverified evidence.

End the answer with a "Sources:" section linking every relevant result as [Title](URL).

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

definitions.name: TaskStop
definitions.description: Stops a running background task by id and reports whether the stop landed. A task that has already finished is not an error: the answer says how and when it ended and where its output file is, and nothing is stopped.

task_id.description: The id of the background task to stop

shell_id.description: Deprecated: use task_id instead. The id of the background shell to stop.

definitions.name: AskUserQuestion
definitions.description: Ask structured multiple-choice questions and return the user's answers.

id.description: Stable id of the question in the answer; defaults from its position

decisionId.description: Key of the question's interview record (mercury://interview/<session>/<decisionId>); defaults when omitted

question.description: Question text; phrase for multi-select when applicable

id.description: Stable id of the option in the answer; defaults from its position

label.description: Concise 1-5 word label for this option

description.description: What choosing this option means or implies

preview.description: Rendered when the option is focused (host-format dependent)

options.description: Mutually exclusive unless multiSelect; an Other free-text answer is supplied automatically

multiSelect.description: Allow several answers to this question

definitions.name: Skill
definitions.description: Runs a skill by name, with optional arguments — inline in this conversation, or in a forked crewmate when the skill declares one. The skills on offer ride in system-reminder messages in this conversation; a user's "slash command" or "/something" means a skill.

skill.description: The skill's name, or "<extension>:<skill>" for an extension skill

args.description: Optional arguments passed to the skill

definitions.name: ApolloReview
definitions.description: Presents the closing review card of a completed Apollo pre-flight spec to the user — the plain-language summary, the blockers, the spec files and where the prototype will run — and returns the answer they chose. With no blockers the card offers three answers: a plain yes moves the session out of Apollo Mode into the build posture (the autonomous mode when available, otherwise edit-approved) and starts the build at once; yes-but-ask-first starts it with each edit asking for confirmation; a hold keeps the session and the spec drafts in Apollo Mode. With blockers present nothing changes hands.

summary.description: The review of the completed spec in plain language; a technical term only beside its plain meaning

blockers.description: What still prevents a one-shot prototype, each with a short comment; empty asks the user to begin the build

specFiles.description: Absolute paths of the spec files the interview produced

runNote.description: Where and how the prototype will be run, one plain line

definitions.name: LspRead
definitions.description: Asks the language servers about code and returns their answer: where a symbol is defined, every reference to it, its type and documentation, its callers and callees, the symbols in a file or across the workspace, the current errors and warnings in files, and each server's state, restarts, last error and what it can answer. It only reads.

operation.description: goToDefinition, findReferences, hover, goToImplementation, typeDefinition, incomingCalls and outgoingCalls read filePath, line and character; documentSymbol reads filePath; workspaceSymbol reads query and limit, with filePath choosing the server; diagnostics reads paths or filePath; serverStatus reads filePath or nothing. Other arguments are ignored

line.description: The symbol's 1-based line, as Read shows it

character.description: The symbol's 1-based character on that line

query.description: workspaceSymbol: a symbol name or part of one

limit.description: workspaceSymbol: the most symbols to return (default 50)

paths.description: diagnostics: files or directories (a directory stands for the files under it that a server covers), at most 50

definitions.name: LspRename
definitions.description: Renames a symbol everywhere the language server sees it — the declaration, imports, re-exports and every reference in every file, never a comment or a string. Without apply it returns the edits (file, line:character range, old → new text, up to 40 per file with the rest counted) and a plan token and writes nothing; with apply: true and that plan it writes exactly those edits and returns the error and warning count the server reports for the first file written.

filePath.description: Absolute path of a file holding an occurrence of the symbol

line.description: The occurrence's 1-based line, as Read shows it

character.description: The occurrence's 1-based character on that line

newName.description: What the symbol is called after the rename

apply.description: true writes; omitted or false returns the edits and a plan token and writes nothing

plan.description: With apply: the plan token the preview returned (lsp-…); exactly those edits are written, and none if a touched file changed since the preview. Without a plan, apply writes only when this session has read the touched lines of every file as they stand

definitions.name: LspMoveSymbol
definitions.description: Moves a top-level declaration — function, class, interface, type, enum or variable — into another file, with every import of it rewritten by the language server; TypeScript and JavaScript only. Without apply it returns the edits (file, line:character range, old → new text, up to 40 per file with the rest counted) and a plan token and writes nothing; with apply: true and that plan it writes exactly those edits.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the file that holds the declaration

line.description: The declaration name's 1-based line, as Read shows it

character.description: The declaration name's 1-based character on that line

targetPath.description: The file the declaration moves into: created when absent, appended to when present

apply.description: true writes; omitted or false returns the edits and a plan token and writes nothing

plan.description: With apply: the plan token the preview returned (lsp-…); exactly those edits are written, and none if a touched file changed since the preview. Without a plan, apply writes only when this session has read the touched lines of every file as they stand

definitions.name: LspMoveFile
definitions.description: Moves or renames a file or a directory and updates every import of it that a language server knows about; a file type no server covers moves without import updates, and the preview says so. Without apply it returns the import edits and, when there are any, a plan token, and moves nothing; with apply: true and that plan it writes the edits and moves the path.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the file or directory to move

newPath.description: Where it goes; must not exist yet

apply.description: true moves the path and writes the import edits; omitted or false returns the edits and, when there are any, a plan token, and moves nothing

plan.description: With apply: the plan token the preview returned, when it returned one; nothing is written or moved if a touched file changed since the preview

definitions.name: LspCodeAction
definitions.description: Lists what the language server offers at a position or range — quick fixes for the errors there, refactors such as extract and convert, and whole-file source actions — each with a stable id; with an action chosen it returns that action's edits and a plan token and writes nothing; with apply: true and that plan it writes exactly those edits. Only edits are applied, never a server command.

line.description: 1-based line where the range starts, as Read shows it

endLine.description: 1-based line where the range ends (default: line)

endCharacter.description: 1-based character where the range ends (default: character)

kind.description: Only actions of this kind: quickfix, refactor or a sub-kind, or a source.* kind (source.organizeImports, source.addMissingImports, source.removeUnusedImports, source.removeUnused); with apply: true and exactly one action left, that one is applied

actionId.description: The id of an action from the list; ids are stable across listings

actionIndex.description: The position of an action in the current list; positions shift between listings

apply.description: true writes; omitted or false returns the edits and a plan token and writes nothing

plan.description: With apply: the plan token the preview returned (lsp-…); exactly those edits are written, and none if a touched file changed since the preview. Without a plan, apply writes only when this session has read the touched lines of every file as they stand

definitions.name: LspFormat
definitions.description: Formats a file, or only a range of its lines, with the language server that owns formatting for its type — ruff for Python when it is installed — or sorts and prunes its imports. Without apply it returns the edits (file, line:character range, old → new text, up to 40 per file with the rest counted) and a plan token and writes nothing; with apply: true and that plan it writes exactly those edits.

line.description: First line to format (1-based); omit line and endLine to format the whole file

organizeImports.description: true sorts and prunes the imports instead of formatting

apply.description: true writes; omitted or false returns the edits and a plan token and writes nothing

plan.description: With apply: the plan token the preview returned (lsp-…); exactly those edits are written, and none if a touched file changed since the preview. Without a plan, apply writes only when this session has read the touched lines of every file as they stand

definitions.name: LspRequest
definitions.description: Sends one raw request to the language server for a file — any method, with params as JSON text — and returns its raw answer; nothing it returns is applied.

filePath.description: Absolute path of a file the server covers

method.description: The LSP method. Methods that edit are not accepted: textDocument/rename, textDocument/codeAction, codeAction/resolve, textDocument/formatting, textDocument/rangeFormatting, workspace/executeCommand, workspace/willRenameFiles, workspace/applyEdit

params.description: The request params as JSON text, sent exactly as given; textDocument and position are not filled in

definitions.name: Inspect
definitions.description:
Read Mercury records by reference. Returns bounded pages and distinct absent, expired or unavailable states. Omitting the id lists objects of that kind.

Kinds: agent, artifact, evidence, execution, file, git, health, ide, journey, mission, models, owner, project, receipt, repo, run, seat, service, structure, task, test, transaction, transcript, workbench, workflow.
models — mercury://models lists reachable models live; mercury://models/known lists this build's pin tables, not reachability.
seat — mercury://seat gives this turn's model, effort, posture and session engine history with switch times.

ref.description: mercury://<kind>[/<id>][?lines=A-B&q=text&cursor=N&limit=N&child=name]. Selectors choose a line range, substring filter, page or named child.

definitions.name: Service
definitions.description: Manage named long-running project processes and their readiness, logs and input. Returns current state and cursored output from one ordered stdout/stderr log; wait reports readiness or unmet conditions.

op.description: Service operation; restart reuses the saved start specification.

name.description: Project-scoped service name (all ops except list)

command.description: start: the executable (argv[0] — no shell parsing)

readiness.description: start: readiness conditions — log regex · tcp port (host 127.0.0.1) · http url (GET, status 200) · file path · stable ms (the process alive that long).

restart.description: start: auto-restart policy (default never; bounded backoff, explicit stop always suppresses)

lifecycle.description: start: session dies with this session (default); project survives it and can be stopped from any session on this project.

pty.description: start: use a pseudo-terminal; screen bytes become log lines and input sends keystrokes. Default false uses a pipe.

mode.description: input: write sends exact text and control bytes; submit adds Enter (default); eof ends input and ignores text.

timeoutMs.description: wait: readiness deadline in ms (default 30000, min 100, max 300000); input: how long to wait for the service's reply in ms (default 500, min 100, max 30000); a value outside the bounds is clamped to them and the result says so

cursor.description: logs: byte cursor from a previous read (omit for the tail)

text.description: input: text sent to stdin; only the spawning session can send it.

definitions.name: Debug
definitions.description: Drives a real debugger over the Debug Adapter Protocol: launch or attach, breakpoints, stepping, stacks, scopes, variables, evaluate, memory and raw adapter requests, in named sessions that belong to this agent and are reaped when its run ends. A stop comes back with its reason, thread and top frames; a wait that outlasts timeoutMs comes back with the debuggee still running. launch, attach and customRequest ask permission.

session.description: Session name (default "main"); a re-launch on the same name replaces that session

adapter.description: launch/attach: adapter key; inferred from the program extension when omitted

program.description: launch: the program to run. attach: the running program to join

stopOnEntry.description: launch: stop at the first instruction

timeoutMs.description: Milliseconds to wait for the next stop (default 10000, no cap)

lines.description: breakpoints: the lines, replacing the file's set on every session; [] clears it

breakpoints.description: breakpoints: rows with a condition, hit count or log message, in place of lines; replaces the file's set on every session, [] clears it

condition.description: Stop only when this expression holds

logMessage.description: Log this instead of stopping (a logpoint)

port.description: attach: the debuggee's listening debug port; alone, it selects the python adapter

method.description: customRequest: the DAP command, sent verbatim

body.description: customRequest: the request arguments as JSON text

functions.description: functionBreakpoints: names, or {name, condition?, hitCondition?} rows; the set reaches every session of the tree and a child session started later, and [] clears it everywhere

name.description: The function to break on entry of

condition.description: Stop only when this expression holds

dataBreakpoints.description: dataBreakpoints: the variables to stop on; replaces the set, [] clears it

variablesReference.description: The scope or structure holding the variable (from scopes/variables)

frameId.description: Frame for an expression-style name, when the adapter resolves by frame

accessType.description: Stop on read, write (default) or both

condition.description: Stop only when this expression holds

instructionBreakpoints.description: instructionBreakpoints: the instruction addresses to stop at; replaces the set, [] clears it

instructionReference.description: A stack frame's [ip …] or an address from disassemble

condition.description: Stop only when this expression holds

memoryReference.description: disassemble/readMemory/writeMemory: a memory reference (a stack frame's [ip …] or a variable's [memory …])

offset.description: disassemble/readMemory/writeMemory: byte offset from the memory reference

data.description: writeMemory: the bytes to write, base64-encoded

allowPartial.description: writeMemory: accept a partial write when only part of the range is writable

instructionCount.description: disassemble: instructions to decode (default 16, at most 64)

threadId.description: Thread for stack/continue/step/pause (defaults to the stopped thread)

frameId.description: Frame for scopes/evaluate/completions (from stack); evaluate defaults to the top frame of the thread that stopped last

depth.description: stack: number of frames to return (default 20)

expression.description: evaluate: the expression, run in the debuggee

context.description: evaluate: the context the adapter evaluates in (default "repl"; "watch" for a side-effect-free read, "hover" for a symbol under the cursor, "clipboard" for a copyable value, "variables" for a variables-view value)

filters.description: exceptionBreakpoints: filter ids to arm; omitted, the adapter's filters are listed

sourceReference.description: source: the sourceReference from a stack frame or loadedSources (>0)

name.description: setVariable: the variable name inside variablesReference

text.description: completions: the partial expression to complete

definitions.name: Test
definitions.description: Runs the project's tests from their framework's own records and returns the argv that ran, the counts, each failure with its test name, file and line, available diagnostics and a durable record at mercury://test/run/<id> (mercury://test/latest and mercury://test/failures follow the newest run); output past the result goes to an artifact reference. discover lists the test node ids or the runner profiles the manifest declares; run executes the suite, one path, one node, the tests related to the changed files, or one profile; rerunFailed repeats the failures the latest run recorded; debug starts one test under its language's debugger, stops on the test's first line and leaves that debugger session open; report reads a record. Python projects run under pytest or unittest, others under the runner their manifest declares (node-test, vitest, jest, cargo, go). A run whose exit code disagrees with its records says so in a verdictNote; a selection that matched no test returns zero counts, which is neither a pass nor a failure.

framework.description: The runner. Default: in a Python project pytest when it is importable, else unittest; otherwise the one runner the manifest declares (package.json → node-test, vitest or jest · Cargo.toml → cargo · go.mod → go)

path.description: run: one test file or directory. A path outside the session project selects that project (its nearest manifest or Python root) for every op, and the result names the project it read

node.description: run: one test node id (pytest: file::test_name · unittest: module.Class.test). debug: required, the test to debug (node-test, vitest, jest: file::name, or a bare name from the latest run's case rows · go: TestName, TestName/subtest or dir::TestName · cargo: module::path::test_name)

changed.description: run: only the tests related to the working tree's changed files (vitest related · jest --findRelatedTests · the changed test files for node-test and pytest · the changed packages for go; not available for cargo)

profile.description: run: a runner-profile id (rp-…) from discover

session.description: debug: the name of the debugger session the call leaves open (default "test")

file.description: debug: the source file for breakpoints

runId.description: report: a run id (default: the latest run)

definitions.name: Eval
definitions.description:
Runs one code cell in a retained Python or JavaScript runtime and returns its value, output and errors. State is kept per agent, language and working directory, and reaped after 15 minutes idle; cells in one message run in order. Helpers inside a cell call session tools, launch a crewmate, run a model completion, read and write files and display rich output; their signatures arrive on first use.
- `py` — Python 3.14.7 (python3)
- `js` — Node v24.21.0

language.description: The retained runtime this cell runs in.

title.description: Short human title for the cell card.

timeoutSeconds.description: Runtime budget in seconds: default 30, at most 600; 0 disables; time inside tool calls and permission waits never counts.

reset.description: Recreate this language's kernel first (the other language keeps its state).

definitions.name: Launch
definitions.description: Lists and runs the project's launch profiles: .vscode/launch.json configurations, the detected Python tests and a rerun of their last failures, CMake presets, Godot scenes, package.json, Cargo.toml and go.mod test and build scripts, and Unity and Blender headless recipes (printed, never run). A profile's id (lp-…) follows its content, so a changed source gives a new id. list returns every profile and the skipped launch.json configurations with why; inspect returns a profile's payload, origin, dropped fields and the call it runs as; debug starts it under its debugger in a debugger session that replaces a live session of the same name, with breakpoints from file and lines; run starts it without a debugger, and a program still running after 15 s stays in a debugger session; test runs its tests; build runs its CMake configure and build or the runner's build script; last returns this session's last Launch action. debug and test return the run's own result with the call it ran as.

profile.description: The profile id (lp-…) from list; required for inspect, debug, run, test and build

session.description: The debugger session for debug (default "main") or for a still-running run (default "launch")

file.description: debug: the source file for breakpoints

definitions.name: Transaction
definitions.description: Shows or closes the record Mercury keeps of the work in this project: every change a tool lands and every check that runs — tests, builds, type checks and lints — is recorded as it happens, nothing is written to it by hand, and a record starts with the first change after the last finish; where the project has no test or build setup, reading each changed file back in full counts as the check. status returns what changed, which checks ran after the last change and whether "completed" can land now. finish closes and saves the record with its verdict: "completed" lands only when the newest check after the last change passed and no later change attempt failed or ended indeterminate, and the record stays open otherwise; "failed" and "abandoned" always land.

op.description: status: show the record · finish: close and save it

unresolved.description: finish: real remaining doubt, kept word for word on the record

definitions.name: Structure
definitions.description: Query JS/TS/JSX/TSX syntax by node kind and preview targeted codemods. Queries return match ids; previews return plans without writing. Apply checks unchanged sources and valid syntax before writing atomically.

name.description: query: name filter — exact or glob with *

files.description: query: file globs relative to the project root; .js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs/.ts/.mts/.cts/.tsx files only.

queryId.description: preview/explain: the query record (sq-…); defaults to the latest

replacement.description: preview replace · insert-before · insert-after: new text; $TEXT in replace is the original node. Inserts land on their own line at the node boundary.

to.description: preview rename/replace-callee: new name/callee. rename changes the token, not every symbol reference.

newModule.description: preview replace-import: the new module specifier

newValue.description: preview set-value: the new property value text

matchId.description: explain: match id (sm-…) whose AST ancestry to return.

definitions.name: AstSearch
definitions.description: Searches code by its syntax: a pattern written as code in the target language, with meta-variables for the parts that vary, is matched against each file's parsed tree, so strings and comments never match. Matches come in file order as file:line:col with the matched code and every capture, 50 at a time by default with the rest counted; a file that does not parse is named.

pattern.description: One complete node written as code in the target language: a fragment that is not standalone goes inside its container, and a declaration carries every part it has (a declared return type as ": $_" in TypeScript, " -> $_" in Python). $NAME matches one node and captures it; $$$NAME matches zero or more siblings and captures them; $_ and $$$ match without capturing. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, a repeated name must match identical code, and spacing, line breaks and comments never matter.

path.description: A file or a directory; the working directory when omitted. Dot-files and dot-folders, node_modules, dist, build, out, coverage, venv, __pycache__, vendor, target and the root .gitignore's plain entries are skipped unless named here.

glob.description: Only the files matching this glob, relative to path; {a,b} lists alternatives.

lang.description: One grammar for every file, instead of each file's extension deciding; this build carries: python · go · rust · javascript · typescript · tsx · bash · c-sharp · cpp · css · java · php · ruby · powershell · ini · regex; a file without a grammar is skipped and counted.

mode.description: "matches" (the default) lists each match with its captures; "count" tallies matches per file

limit.description: Matches to return (default 50, max 200); the rest are counted.

offset.description: Matches to skip before the window. Default 0.

definitions.name: AstEdit
definitions.description: Rewrites every match of a syntax pattern across files as one change: each match is replaced by the rewrite built from its captures. A call without apply is a dry run that returns the unified diff per file and a plan token and writes nothing; the same call with apply: true and that plan writes the change after the edit permission ask, atomically with rollback and a re-read of every file, and returns one change receipt naming each file's new anchor.

pattern.description: One complete node written as code in the target language: a fragment that is not standalone goes inside its container, and a declaration carries every part it has (a declared return type as ": $_" in TypeScript, " -> $_" in Python). $NAME matches one node and captures it; $$$NAME matches zero or more siblings and captures them; $_ and $$$ match without capturing. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, a repeated name must match identical code, and spacing, line breaks and comments never matter.

rewrite.description: The replacement, as code in the target language: $NAME and $$$NAME insert the captured source verbatim, and every meta-variable here must be captured by the pattern ($_ and $$$ cannot be inserted); "" deletes each matched node, and a node that owns its line takes the line with it.

path.description: A file or a directory; the working directory when omitted. Dot-files and dot-folders, node_modules, dist, build, out, coverage, venv, __pycache__, vendor, target and the root .gitignore's plain entries are skipped unless named here.

glob.description: Only the files matching this glob, relative to path; {a,b} lists alternatives.

lang.description: One grammar for every file, instead of each file's extension deciding; this build carries: python · go · rust · javascript · typescript · tsx · bash · c-sharp · cpp · css · java · php · ruby · powershell · ini · regex; a file without a grammar is skipped and counted.

apply.description: Omitted or false: a dry run returning the diff and a plan token, nothing written. true: write the change; needs the plan from the dry run.

plan.description: The plan token (ae-…) the dry run returned; apply refuses when a file, the pattern, the rewrite or the scope differs from that dry run.

definitions.name: ChangeSet
definitions.description: Applies one set of edits, moves and deletions across existing text files as a whole: every member is checked against its read anchor before the first write and one operator decision covers the set; a drifted or invalid member refuses the whole set and nothing is written. preview builds a plan (cs-…) without writing; apply writes a plan or the changes given, verified by reread, and names any path it could not settle; status and discard manage a plan. Up to 16 files a set; a plan lives 30 minutes.

changes.description: preview / apply: the file members, one per existing text file

file_path.description: Absolute path to an existing text file

expected_anchor.description: The bare fa:… or ra:… value inside the latest "(anchor: …)" for this file — a Read, or an Edit or Write result — without the wrapper

hunks.description: Disjoint line-addressed hunks against the anchored snapshot; a member carries hunks or edits, a move optionally, a delete neither

lines.description: 1-based original line ("12") or inclusive range ("12-18") of the anchored snapshot

replace.description: Replacement body; "" deletes the range; with insert, the inserted body

insert.description: Insert beside the single anchor line instead of replacing it

edits.description: Disjoint exact-string edits against the anchored snapshot, instead of hunks

old_string.description: The exact text to replace; unique in the file unless replace_all

new_string.description: The text to replace it with; "" deletes old_string

op.description: "edit" (default) applies the hunks or edits; "delete" removes the file; "move" renames it to new_path after any hunks or edits

new_path.description: move: the absolute destination path, which must not exist

plan_id.description: apply / status / discard: a plan id (cs-…) from a prior preview

definitions.name: Git
definitions.description: Inspect local repositories and hosted review/check data, stage exact changes, or preview and apply commit groups. Returns bounded records and stable hunk/plan ids. It does not fetch, push, rewrite history or discard working-tree content.

cwd.description: the folder to run in (default: the session folder). The repository containing it is used; when it is not inside one but holds exactly one repository directly below it, that one is used

ref.description: diff: commit SHA or A..B range; fileAtRef/tree: source ref.

groups.description: plan: proposed commit groups in dependency order; previews without committing.

files.description: exact repo-relative paths (a file belongs to at most one group)

hunks.description: optional per-file exact hunk-id subsets (gh-… from op:"diff")

message.description: the commit message for this group

checks.description: checks associated with this group (recorded on the plan)

planId.description: Plan id (gp-…). apply creates commits after checking the tree digest; earlier groups stay committed if a later group fails. verify reports applicability and created commits.

files.description: Exact repo-relative paths to stage or restore; restore unstages without changing working files.

path.description: resolve: conflicted path to resolve and stage; fileAtRef: file; tree: optional directory.

content.description: resolve: explicit resolved content (instead of take)

pr.description: reviewContext/prDiff: compose against this PR instead of the current branch (needs the gh session)

findings.description: reviewRecord: the typed findings (empty = an honest no-findings review; inspected required)

class.description: verified defect · open question · non-blocking polish

path.description: exact repo-relative path inside the reviewed diff set

inspected.description: reviewRecord: what was actually inspected (required when findings is empty)

searchKind.description: hostSearch: what to search on the host

query.description: hostSearch: the search query (GitHub search syntax)

limit.description: hostSearch/runs: result bound (search ≤50 default 10 · runs ≤20 default 10)

file.description: prDiff: one changed file's path — pages that file's diff (omit for the file list)

page.description: prDiff: 0-based page of the selected file (80 diff lines per page)

run.description: Workflow-run id. runs inspects one run; runWatch returns immediately and settles on its observed conclusion.

cancel.description: runWatch: true cancels the live watch for `run` instead of starting one

definitions.name: Journey
definitions.description: Run a local application check across services, HTTP, commands, files and diagnostics. Returns per-step evidence, cleanup outcome and a verdict; the first failure skips remaining steps.

pattern.description: Regular expression polled against the service logs.

files.description: Files to check for parse-level diagnostics.

jsonPath.description: Dot-separated keys from the last http.request's JSON response root (data.items.0.id); compared as text.

cleanup.description: stop-started stops journey-started services after the run (default); keep leaves them running until this session ends.

definitions.name: Browser
definitions.description: Drive one isolated browser session per agent through the bundled driver. Returns page observations, action results and screenshots. Opening a new origin or first acting on a crossed-to origin asks; reads never ask. Grants belong to this agent and end with its session.

url.description: open: the URL to navigate to (http/https)

selector.description: Element target: CSS, aria/<name>[role="<role>"] with exact accessible name, text/<substring>, xpath/<expr>, or host >>> inner across shadow roots. Omitted: type uses focus; extract uses the whole page.

frame.description: Frame index from extract (0 is main), or a unique URL substring. Acts use that frame origin, including secret fills.

force.description: click: dispatch a DOM click to a covered selector target.

x.description: click: viewport x for a point click (with y; selector wins when both given)

y.description: click: viewport y for a point click (with x)

text.description: type: the characters to type · waitFor: the page text to await

secretRef.description: type: operator-registered UPPER_SNAKE secret name, with selector. Credential fields require this instead of text. The value stays out of the conversation; each secret-and-origin pairing needs separate approval.

clear.description: type: clear the field first (selector targets only)

dy.description: scroll: pixel delta (positive scrolls down) when no selector is given

timeoutMs.description: waitFor and selector actions/reads: deadline in ms (default 10000, cap 30000).

state.description: waitFor selector: visible (default), attached even if hidden, or hidden/removed.

mode.description: extract: text = innerText (default) · tree = accessibility-tree projection

values.description: select: option values to choose (visible-label fallback); multiple only on a multiple select

key.description: press: a navigation/edit key — Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown (printable characters go through type)

modifiers.description: press: modifiers held around the key

buildId.description: provision: exact Chrome-for-Testing build (default current stable).

offset.description: extract: character offset for the text window.

fullPage.description: screenshot: capture the full scroll height (default viewport)

definitions.name: Computer
definitions.description:
Operate the desktop by screenshot coordinates or accessibility targets. Coordinates are pixels of its last screenshot; refresh after frame changes. Trees use [n] role "title" value rows. Terminal captures return accessibility text by default. Text fields: fill (target/ref) sets the value and reads it back; fields lists the controls.

The first act of a session asks once; tree/find/read/wait-until share its grant. Other reads never ask. Operator typing pauses automation; esc/ctrl+c releases input.

After a click whose effect you assume (a dialog, a focus change, a page), wait with until; a sequence stops at its timeout. After the same act twice with an unchanged result, read the screen before acting again.

x.description: Last-screenshot x coordinate; paired with y.

y.description: Last-screenshot y coordinate; paired with x.

text.description: type or fill: at most 4000 characters; only newline and tab control characters.

key.description: Key chord: Enter, Escape, Tab, Space, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, F1–F12 or one character, with cmd/ctrl/alt/shift joined by +.

durationMs.description: hold: 50–5000 ms; wait: default 1000, 5000 with until, maximum 10000 ms.

display.description: Display number; omitted, the front window. Also applies to acts with capture:true.

settleMs.description: Post-action delay in ms, default 300, capped at 5000; not a readiness check.

capture.description: Return an image after an act. A sequence returns one final image; screenshot steps capture in place. wait-until captures on a match. false suppresses images.

full.description: Capture a display instead of the front window; also applies to acts with capture:true.

pixels.description: Return terminal pixels rather than accessibility text.

scale.description: Capture scale; default 0.5 for windows, 1 for displays/regions.

depth.description: Tree depth; default 12, clamped at 32. Targets use the cap by default.

limit.description: Tree rows; default 400, clamped at 2000. Targets use the cap by default.

target.description: Accessibility target: exact role/name, substring text; nth selects a 1-based match.

ref.description: Node number from the latest tree or find; stale once the list changes. Choose ref, target or x/y.

root.description: Tree root: node number or accessibility target.

clipboard.description: read: use clipboard text with separate consent instead of target/ref.

focusApp.description: Bring a running application forward by name or bundle id; capture screenshots after.

toTarget.description: drag: destination accessibility target instead of toX/toY.

until.description: wait: text/title/URL substring, role/name, dialog: true or focus (a role); gone waits for removal. Put it after a click whose effect you assume.

scope.description: Tree scope: window by default; app includes menus and windows.

verify.description: Compare trees after acting; reports change, not task success.

captcha.description: Ask the operator before acting on a visible challenge.

path.description: file: absolute path of the file to upload through the native dialog.

steps.description: Non-nested sequence; stops at first failure, a wait-until timeout included. Capture, region, scale and settleMs belong on the sequence. Step fields have the same meanings as the top-level fields.

target.description: role/name exact; text substring; unique match

definitions.name: EnterWorktree
definitions.description: Creates an isolated git worktree under the project's `.mercury/worktrees/` on a new branch from the current head — outside a repository the configured hooks provide the isolation — and moves this session's working directory into it, on the user's word "worktree" only; a session already in a worktree it created stays where it is. The session ends with a keep-or-remove prompt for the worktree.

name.description: Worktree name: letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes within each slash-delimited segment; at most 64 characters. Omitted ⇒ a generated name.

definitions.name: ExitWorktree
definitions.description: Ends the worktree session this session started and restores its original working directory, on the user's explicit ask; a worktree created by hand or by a previous session is untouched, and with no active worktree session the call says so and touches nothing. keep leaves the worktree directory and its branch on disk, and a tmux session attached to the worktree keeps running with its name returned for the user; remove deletes both and kills that tmux session. Caches that depend on the working directory are cleared.

action.description: "keep" leaves the worktree directory and its branch on disk for later; "remove" deletes both.

discard_changes.description: With remove: true discards the worktree's uncommitted files and unmerged commits with it, on the user's word; false (the default) removes only a worktree that has none.

definitions.name: Checkpoint
definitions.description: Marks the current conversation state as the checkpoint a later rewind restores, before an exploratory detour whose transcript need not stay in context; the goal is echoed back at the rewind. One checkpoint is active at a time, and a run that ends with it still active gets a settle warning. The pair touches the model context only: files, git state and the operator's visible transcript are never changed by it.

goal.description: What the exploration sets out to learn or attempt; echoed back at the rewind.

definitions.name: Rewind
definitions.description: Restores the model context to the active checkpoint at the end of this turn: the next model call sees the context from before the exploration plus the report, and everything between the checkpoint and the rewind leaves the model context. The operator's transcript keeps the exploration visible; files and git state are untouched.

report.description: The one artifact that survives the rewind, written as a handoff: findings, decisions, exact paths, next steps. Required, non-empty after trim.

definitions.name: SendMessage
definitions.description: Delivers a message to a running crewmate of this session; it never starts work, and a crewmate that has finished is refused. Plain output reaches no crewmate: words travel only as messages. A running crewmate reads the message at its next tool boundary, else at the end of its turn; the main agent reads it the same way, and between turns it starts a turn for it. A message relayed to you is already rendered to the user.

to.description: The crewmate to send to: the id its launch receipt names or the name its launch gave it (a name two launches carried reaches the newest); "main" from a background crewmate reaches the agent that launched it

definitions.name: CrewBoard
definitions.description: Read or post on the shared crew board. Every post is visible to all enrolled seats; addressing controls delivery, not privacy. Owner posts carry the operator's authority; other posts are peer task data. Returns oldest-first events or a posting receipt. Posts arrive at each seat's next boundary.

op.description: Read/post events; lead-only swarm_team assigns a team and swarm_captain appoints its captain.

team.description: Assignment team, or read filter; omitted on read, the general timeline.

clientOpId.description: Post retry key. Reuse only for an identical retry.

kind.description: Post type. An ask/blocker to @main or @all, or a result/answer/correction to @main by name, wakes an idle lead in one batched turn; other posts do not.

corrects.description: Earlier event id for a correction; appends without erasing it.

since.description: Read after this sequence; 0 rereads from the start. Omitted, continue the enrollment cursor and skip already-presented events; skippedSeen counts them since enrollment.

acknowledge.description: Event ids to acknowledge; fetching does not acknowledge.

definitions.name: ResumeCrewmate
definitions.description: Gives a crewmate of this session its next turn: the message. A crewmate that has finished (completed, failed or stopped) is resumed from its transcript in the background with its full context; a running one reads the message at its next tool boundary, or, with interrupt: true, its turn is cut after its partial transcript is saved and the new turn starts. A resumed turn is a paid turn of that crewmate; its completion notice reaches the main agent, and a crewmate launched with an output schema keeps its StructuredOutput tool for the resumed turn.

to.description: The crewmate to resume: the id its launch receipt names or the name its launch gave it, running or finished; a name two launches carried reaches the newest

message.description: Its next turn: what to do, written as you would brief it

model.description: Model for the resumed turn of a finished crewmate; omitted, its recorded model stays. Read mercury://models for available ids.

effort.description: Effort for the resumed turn; omitted, its recorded effort stays. Max is admitted; an unsupported lower tier is refused, not clamped.

interrupt.description: Interrupt a running turn and start this message as its next turn; omitted or false, deliver it at the next tool boundary.

definitions.name: Workflow
definitions.description: Run a deterministic JavaScript script coordinating crewmates. Returns a task ID immediately and notifies on completion. Launch only on the user's workflow request or an executing skill's direction.

name.description: Saved or built-in workflow name; used when scriptPath is absent.

args.description: JSON value exposed as args, verbatim; omitted, undefined.

scriptPath.description: Path to a saved workflow, selected before name.

resumeFromRunId.description: Prior run ID from this session, after that run stops.

definitions.name: Sleep
definitions.description: Waits the given seconds without holding a shell process, returning early when the user interrupts, new input arrives, or the crewmates and background commands it tracks finish; the result says which and reports the time actually waited. Periodic check-in prompts wrapped in <tick> tags may arrive during the wait, each a nudge to look for useful work before sleeping on. Every wake is a model call, and the prompt cache lapses after 5 minutes of idleness.

seconds.description: How many seconds to wait before returning (min 1, max 3600; a value outside the bounds is clamped to them and the result says so).

definitions.name: CronCreate
definitions.description: Puts a prompt on this session's clock — one run after a delay or at a set time, or a repeating cron schedule — kept by the Mercury daemon on this session's record and fired into the session, parked or not, on this session's model and account; the operator sees every schedule on the /saturn board. The call waits for the daemon and returns the schedule's id and its fire time in local time and UTC; an answer that is not "Scheduled" says whether the request may have landed and how to find out. A fire lands within 30 seconds after its time, only while the session is idle; one the sign-in cannot serve is held with a receipt until /logins releases it, one due while the machine slept runs late or, past the catch-up window, is recorded as missed, and a schedule outlives interrupts.

cron.description: Repeating: five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) in local time, never UTC; numbers, *, ranges (1-5), lists (1,15) and steps (*/10), no names. Pass exactly one of cron, at, delayMinutes.

at.description: One run at a local date and time, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" (an offset such as "Z" or "+01:00" is accepted); must be in the future.

delayMinutes.description: One run this many minutes from now (1 to 525600); it fires on the next whole minute at or after the delay.

prompt.description: What runs at each fire, 1 to 20,000 characters, stored with the schedule and delivered verbatim with no memory of why it was set: self-contained, no secrets.

recurring.description: With cron only. Default true; false runs once at the next match, then removes itself (for one run prefer at or delayMinutes).

onParked.description: What a fire does when the session is parked: 'wake' (default) reactivates the session and delivers; 'queue' holds the fire for the session's own next wake.

title.description: A short name for the schedule (one line of at most 200 characters), shown on its rows in the chat and the list in place of the id; the name the user gave the task, when they gave one.

definitions.name: CronDelete
definitions.description: Cancels a schedule on this session's record by id; the removal travels on the session's next facts beat and is receipted.

id.description: The schedule id to cancel (eight hex characters)

definitions.name: CronList
definitions.description: Lists this session's schedules as the daemon last pushed them: id, timing, one-shot or recurring, fire-into-session or session-birth, next fire, paused state. A schedule answered "Queued, not confirmed" at creation appears once the daemon applies it.

definitions.name: ScheduleWakeup
definitions.description: Wakes this session once, after 60–3600 seconds, with the prompt given. The wake fires on a minute boundary once the session is idle; an operator interruption or stop drops it, a parked session keeps it. A daemon-hosted wake persists with the session; on a bare run it is a timer that ends with the run. It fires once: a loop continues only when the woken prompt schedules the next wake.

delaySeconds.description: Delay in seconds, clamped to 60–3600; the wake fires on the next minute boundary at or after it.

prompt.description: The prompt to enqueue when the wake fires.

reason.description: A short note on why you are waking yourself; it heads the woken prompt and shows on the wake's row.

definitions.name: Monitor
definitions.description: Starts a background watch on a command and delivers each line of its stdout as a notification in the chat while you keep working. A notification is an event of the watch, not a reply from the user, even when it lands while you are waiting for their answer; lines within 200ms fold into one notification, ongoing output is delivered at most once every 30 seconds with its line count and last line, and events that land while the session's usage window is closed are held and delivered together on your first turn after it reopens. The watch ends when the command exits, when its timeout passes with one expiry notice, or, with persistent, when it is stopped or the session ends.

description.description: A few words naming what is watched, shown in each notification.

timeout_ms.description: The watch is killed after this many milliseconds. Default 300000, min 1000, max 3600000; a value outside the bounds is clamped to them and the result says so. Ignored when persistent is true.

persistent.description: true runs the watch for the life of the session, with no timeout, until it is stopped or the session ends.

command.description: The shell command; each stdout line is an event, and its exit ends the watch.

definitions.name: ContextLeft
definitions.description: Reports how full the context window is — the tokens used, the window, the percent, and the tokens left until autocompact folds the transcript — from the same derivation the operator's context gauge reads, each number labelled measured on the wire or estimated from characters. Until this session's first answer the count is unknown, and the answer says so while still naming the window; a window marked ~ is a conservative default, not a figure the provider stated.

definitions.name: RecordConvention
definitions.description: Writes one durable project convention the user stated into the project's instruction estate — MERCURY.md at the project root, born with the first rule when absent, or the guide it points at with an explicit @import — and returns the file it wrote. An exact restatement of an existing rule writes nothing; replaces swaps the existing rule line in place wherever in the estate it lives.

rule.description: The convention, as one plain standing-order sentence

replaces.description: A distinctive substring of the existing rule line this one supersedes; that line is swapped in place

definitions.name: Retain
definitions.description: Store facts in project memory. Returns each item's stored id, already-staged status or refusal reason. Facts stage as pending observations and consolidate into topic pages. Memory is plaintext.

content.description: One durable fact; content and context together may contain at most 2000 characters.

context.description: Where the fact came from (provenance note).

pin.description: Pin the user's exact words as an always-loaded standing rule or preference, when they asked for that lasting rule.

replaces.description: Prior rule id (seq:<n>) the user explicitly replaced; keeps the old wording as history. For a user-requested rule, the user answers a yes/no card first (under sovereign, no card).

definitions.name: Recall
definitions.description: Searches project memory and returns pointers, or reads one full record. A search returns at most 20 pointers, each a stable id (seq:<n> for a fact or ruling, pending:<ts> for a staged row, ledger:<ordinal> for a session or its handoff), a kind (fact · ruling · handoff · session), a one-line title (where it lives, when, from whom, which of your words matched) and footnotes (the session it came from, the ruling it fell under, what it supersedes or was superseded by). A pointer carries no content: open the record with read before you rely on it or quote it. A read returns the entry with its breadcrumb and footnotes; a ledger read is the session's entry and its handoff verbatim. An empty result is flagged elidable: droppable context, not an error. It never writes.

query.description: Words to search for across the pages, the archive, the pending observations and the lineage ledger; a phrase or regex matches literally, otherwise the words of the query are matched. A pointer is an id, a title and footnotes: open one with read to see the record.

read.description: Read one full record by id: seq:<n> (a fact or ruling) · doc:<slug> (a whole page) · pending:<ts> · ledger:<ordinal> (a session's entry and its handoff).

definitions.name: Reflect
definitions.description: Answers a question over project memory: one search for the query, then one bounded model call over the hits, whose synthesis cites the records it uses ([seq N] / [pending N]). A synthesis that cites nothing or invents ids, or a run with no usable model or credentials, returns the raw search instead with the reason. It never writes.

query.description: The question to answer over memory.

definitions.name: Correct
definitions.description: Changes one memory record by id: supersede replaces the fact with a new truth and moves the old one to history with a superseded-by pointer; amend fixes the record's own wording; retract marks it wrong with a reason. A consolidated fact is never deleted: its history stays. A pending row (pending:<ts>) is a draft, not yet a fact: retract strikes it and no history is kept; supersede or amend replaces it with a new pending row, and the new row keeps the old words as its history until consolidation files the fact. A rule the user asked for changes only on their answer to a card the call puts to them with the rule's words as stored and what will happen: Yes runs the op, No returns "the user kept the rule" and nothing changes; under the sovereign permission mode the op runs without the card and its record says so.

op.description: supersede = a new truth; amend = fix the wording, which needs the full record read this session; retract = mark it wrong.

id.description: The record id: seq:<n> for a consolidated row, pending:<ts> for a draft still in the buffer.

content.description: The new or corrected content (supersede, amend).

replacementId.description: supersede only: an existing seq:<n> already carrying the truth, instead of content.

reason.description: Why; every correction carries its reason.

definitions.name: Journal
definitions.description:
Write a brief entry into the journal: where the project is, what the queued backlog is, and what the user asked for in this session, in their words — never Mercury's own standing instructions. Plain words, concise, no longer than a sentence.

- One entry per session; a later call replaces the earlier one. The entry is written to the journal when this session ends. The journal lives in the Mercury home beside the project's memory, never under the project tree, and Mercury never pushes, syncs or shares it. The next session reads the last entry only when the operator's setting (memory.journalOnEntryPage) says so; the operator reads it in /memory.
- The rules Mercury itself works under (its git rules, its constitution) are not the user's constraints: write down only what the user said in this session.

entry.description: A brief entry: where the project is, what the queued backlog is, and what the user asked for in this session, in their words — never Mercury's own standing instructions. Plain words, concise, no longer than a sentence. Under 4000 characters.

definitions.name: ListMcpResources
definitions.description: Lists the resources the connected MCP servers publish, one row each: the server that provides it beside the resource's uri, name and, when given, mimeType and description.

server.description: Restrict the listing to one server, by name

definitions.name: ReadMcpResource
definitions.description: Reads one resource from a connected MCP server and returns its contents as the server sent them: text, or the path binary content was saved to.

server.description: The name of the MCP server to read the resource from

uri.description: The URI of the resource to read

definitions.name: ToolSearch
definitions.description:
Loads the full definitions of deferred tools so they become callable.

Deferred tools are listed in <system-reminder> messages that begin "Deferred tools:", one per line: the name, and what the tool is for when it declares one; keyword search also reads each tool's full description. The result names the admitted tools, and from that request on their complete definitions are in your tool list, no different from the tools the prompt opened with.

query.description: What to load: exact names as "select:<name>,<name>"; or keywords ranked against the deferred roster, where "+word" requires the word (in a tool's name, description or search words) and the other words only rank.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

definitions.name: Document
definitions.description: Create and handle local research documents. Ops: create, convert, merge, split, inspect, cite. output selects the format; source names an input. Writes use file permissions; replacing an output needs its expectedSha256 from inspect. DOI resolution contacts Crossref only when dois is supplied.

output.description: Destination file; extension selects the format

sheet.description: Worksheet name, required when exporting one of several sheets

append.description: Append content to source DOCX, keeping existing parts

pages.description: 1-based page ranges, for example 1-3,7; preserves order

parts.description: split: page ranges and destination per part

rotate.description: Clockwise degrees applied to selected PDF pages

expectedSha256.description: Existing output path to digest from inspect; required for replacement

dois.description: DOIs to resolve through api.crossref.org, only when requested
